metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” bias: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 3–7% to align with historical reversion patterns.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add a “reversal buffer” — reduce forecast by 5–10% in the 3–5 day window following a spike.
- Model underestimates late-period corrections (e.g., last 5–7 days of 30d forecast); adjust downward by 2–5% for final 7 days if true outcome shows downward trend.
